steps.title: Prepare solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required solutions before starting the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Frog Ringer (FR): dissolve 18 mL 5 M NaCl, 2.5 mL 1 M KCl, 1.4 mL 1 M MgCl₂, 1.05 mL 1 M CaCl₂, 5 mL 1 M NaHCO₃, 5 mL 1 M HEPES, 10 mL 1 M glucose, 0.1 mL 1 M EDTA; adjust pH to 7.6 with 0.5 M NaOH; bring to 1 L with MQ water.
Bradford reagent: add 50 mL ethanol (5 %), 100 mg Coomassie Brilliant Blue G‑250, 100 mL 10 % H₃PO₄; fill to 1 L with MQ water.
Mass‑spec solution: dissolve 6.30 g ammonium formate in 1 L MQ water (0.1 M).

steps.title: Acclimatize frogs and cut filter paper
steps.instruction: Acclimatize adult marsh frogs to room temperature and a 12/12 h light cycle for several days, dark‑adapt overnight; punch 1 cm diameter discs from filter paper with a hole punch, handle with gloves/tweezers, store discs in a Petri dish.

steps.title: Extract and segment retina
steps.instruction: In a dim‑red‑light room, decapitate the frog, destroy the brainstem with a thick needle, remove extra‑ocular tissues, hemisect the eye with a scalpel and spring scissors, discard anterior chamber, lens and vitreous; keep the second eye in FR at 4 °C in a light‑tight container; pour several mL FR into a 3 cm Petri dish, submerge the first eye semi‑cup, cut it into 2–4 equal segments as required.

steps.title: Remove pigment epithelium
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, separate each retinal segment from the pigment epithelium with forceps; if epithelium remains, gently shake the segment in FR and remove residual epithelium with tweezers, taking care not to damage the retina.

steps.title: Layer retina on filter disc
steps.instruction: Place a filter‑paper disc into the same Petri dish, position the retina photoreceptor side up on the disc, gently flatten, lift the disc out of the solution so the retina straightens, place the disc on dry filter paper to remove excess liquid (avoid over‑drying).

steps.title: Transfer to 6‑well plate
steps.instruction: Pour 3 mL FR into each well of a 6‑well plate, place each retinal disc into a separate well, keep samples at room temperature in the dark for no more than 10 min before cryofixation.

steps.title: Cool copper cylinders
steps.instruction: Fill the custom light‑isolated cryo‑container with liquid nitrogen, maintain a constant LN₂ level, and pre‑cool the copper cylinders.

steps.title: Pretreat lever pads
steps.instruction: Apply Tissue‑Tek to the lever pads of the illumination device.

steps.title: Light stimulation and cryofixation
steps.instruction: Place the retinal specimen horizontally on the Tissue‑Tek‑treated pad, start the illumination program (λmax = 525 nm) with the selected parameters; after the programmed delay the lever presses the specimen against the polished, LN₂‑cooled copper cylinder; keep the specimen on the cylinder a few minutes to freeze the Tissue‑Tek, then separate it from the pad with a scalpel; transfer the cryofixed specimen to a light‑isolated cryo‑container with LN₂ and store for ≤2 h before cryotome work.

substeps.instruction: Allow the lever pad to warm to room temperature before applying the next sample.
All operations from retina extraction through this step must be performed at room temperature in a dark room under dim red light or infrared observation.

steps.title: Pre‑cool cryotome and tools
steps.instruction: Set the cryotome to –30 °C; pre‑cool tweezers, scalpels, a spatula with thermal insulators, and the custom hollow copper tube (8 mm OD, 0.7 mm wall) with liquid nitrogen before each contact with the sample.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue‑Tek platform
steps.instruction: Freeze Tissue‑Tek onto a flat circular‑patterned chuck to create a specimen platform; trim off the rounded edge of the solidified Tissue‑Tek to obtain a flat surface for sample placement.

steps.title: Fix specimen on platform
steps.instruction: Place the specimen on the platform with the photoreceptor side facing the knife, press it down using the hollow metal tube; add 10 µL Milli‑Q water droplets around the edges of the sample to enhance adhesion by freezing; detach the metal tube and briefly immerse the platform in liquid nitrogen to freeze the droplets.

steps.title: Section retina and collect shavings
steps.instruction: Serially section the retina longitudinally at 10 µm thickness until the orange‑pink photoreceptor layer is completely removed; visually inspect sections and discard white inclusion areas (rod inner segment); collect the cell shavings with a spatula into pre‑cooled microcentrifuge tubes containing 500 µL 0.1 M HCl (to inactivate enzymes).

steps.title: Sonicate cell shavings
steps.instruction: Sonicate the harvested shavings with a liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled ultrasonic tip (2 mm diameter) for 15 s total (pulse mode 3 s on, 1 s off) at 35 % amplitude; keep the suspension at 0.1 °C, aliquot 50 µL for protein assay and 450 µL for LC‑MS/MS; lyophilize the LC‑MS/MS aliquot and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Bradford protein assay
steps.instruction: Prepare BSA standards of various concentrations in 0.1 M HCl; add 200 µL Bradford reagent to each well of a low‑binding 96‑well plate, then add 15 µL of sample or standard (triplicate); measure absorbance at 595 nm; plot a standard curve in Microsoft Excel and calculate protein concentration.

steps.title: Prepare internal standard stock
steps.instruction: Weigh 10 ± 0.1 mg cAMP‑13C5, dissolve in 1 L 0.1 M HCl, store the stock at –20 °C; bring to room temperature before use and dilute to a working solution of 10 ng/mL with 0.1 M HCl.

steps.title: Prepare cAMP and cGMP calibration standards
steps.instruction: Weigh 10 ± 0.1 mg of cAMP and 10 ± 0.1 mg of cGMP separately, dissolve each in 1 L of the internal‑standard solution to obtain stock solutions; prepare calibration solutions of 0.5, 1.0, 5.0, 10.0, 25.0, 100.0 and 200.0 ng/mL by diluting the respective stock with internal‑standard solution.

steps.title: Add internal standard to samples
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of the 10 ng/mL internal‑standard solution to each sample tube; vortex for 15 min at 2000 rpm (room temperature) and sonicate for 15 min at 25 °C, 100 W; centrifuge at 13 100 × g for 5 min; transfer ~40 µL of the supernatant into glass vials for HPLC analysis.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phases for LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Mobile phase A = mass‑spec solution (0.1 M ammonium formate); mobile phase B = acetonitrile.

steps.title: Run LC‑MS/MS chromatography
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a Zorbax SB‑C8 column (150 mm × 4.6 mm × 1.8 µm) with 2 % B at 400 µL/min and 35 °C; inject 20.0 µL sample; apply gradient: 0–2 min 2 % B, 2–8 min linear to 30 % B, 8–9 min hold 30 % B, 9–9.1 min return to 2 % B, 9.1–11 min 2 % B.

steps.title: Set MS/MS detection parameters
steps.instruction: Use negative‑mode ESI, 3.5 kV, mass resolution 35 000, product‑ion scan (PIS), normalized collision energy 20 %, nitrogen as collision gas; monitor transitions: cAMP 328.0452 → 134.0457 (t_R 4.87 min), cGMP 344.0402 → 150.04109 (t_R 4.81 min), IS cAMP‑13C5 328.0452 → 134.0457 (t_R 4.87 min).

steps.title: Process data and quantify analytes
steps.instruction: Process chromatograms in ThermoXcalibur v4.1.31.9 with automatic integration (mass tolerance 10 ppm, Gaussian smoothing 7 points, minimum peak height S/N 2.0, S/N threshold 0.5, Genesis algorithm); identify peaks using NIST MS Search 2.4 and confirm with standards (10 and 100 ng/mL); calculate the area ratio of each analyte to the internal standard; determine concentrations from the calibration curves.
